answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring each identity to emit a unique pulse of sequential proof-of-work that must be confirmed by a zephyr of peer echoes before attestation rights activate. The pulse takes 10 minutes of non-parallel compute per epoch. An attacker forging N identities must generate N separate pulses and collect matching echoes for each, multiplying the CPU time and network latency cost by N while an honest agent pays the serial delay only once and reuses the confirmed pulse, making mass fake identities prohibitively expensive in both energy and time.
